To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the 15.1 MeV state in 12C is strongly mixed with the 12.7 MeV state, with an isospin-mixing amplitude of H01 = (157 ± 35) keV, and that the impulse approximation describes the pion scattering data well.
The isospin mixing of T=0 and T=1 1+ states in 12C was determined by low energy pion scattering.
1) the 1+ isospin mixing is small, 2) the isospin mixing strength is in agreement with the shell model prediction and 3) the isosping mixing is not due to mesonic exchange current contributions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the structure of light nuclei and of the reaction mechanism in the low-energy region.
the structure of the nucleus and its reaction with elementary particles.
the study of nuclear structure by means of low-energy pion-nucleus scattering, and with the development of a new experimental method for the study of nuclear isospin mixing.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the 1+ excitation in 12C is a pure T = 0 state.
isospin mixing is not an essential ingredient in the understanding of pion inelastic scattering to the 12C 1+ doublets at 12.7 MeV and 15.1 MeV.
the impulse approximation is valid for pion scattering to the 1 + states in 12C.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the isospin mixing of 12C is small, the mixing matrix element is of the same order of magnitude as the 1+ excitation energies, but the mixing is not negligible.
the isospin mixing in the 1+ excitation in 12C is not very large and is in agreement with other experimental data.
the 15.11MeV excitation of 12C is predominantly T = 1.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the isospin mixing is not a problem in low-energy pion reactions, at least in 12C.
we have shown that the impulse approximation works well for pion scattering at low energies.
